parts.label: b

parts.label: c

steps.text: Independent Poisson rates add: $2+3=5$ per hour.

title: Choosing a model before calculating a probability
stem: Exactly 40 components are tested independently; each fails with probability 0.03. Separately, faults on a continuous cable occur independently at a uniform rate of 0.4 per metre. The diagram contrasts the two sampling schemes. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Choose a distribution for the component-failure count and calculate the chance of no failures.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Choose a distribution for faults on 5 metres of cable and find the chance of at least two faults.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why using the same distribution merely because both counts are integers is inadequate.

steps.text: A fixed number of independent Bernoulli trials gives $X\sim B(40,0.03)$.
The component count is bounded by 40 with a fixed number of trials.
The cable count is modelled by events along a continuous interval with no fixed maximum; model assumptions matter.
